intent: To illustrate the Sun's overwhelming dominance in mass within the solar system.

units.meaning: The Sun makes up 99.86% of the mass in the solar system.

basis.note: Table row is entity 'share'; intent/narration identifies this as the Sun's mass share. Unit is percent.

accepted_routes: The Sun accounts for 99.86% of the solar system's mass.
The Sun makes up 99.86% of the mass in our solar system.
99.86% of the solar system's mass is the Sun.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A labeled 99.86% value must appear on or for the Sun's mass-share mark.
units.temporal_anchor: final narration clause: 'It makes up 99.86% of the mass in our solar system.'
units.reviewer_question: Is the exact 99.86% value required, or may the video round it to 'almost 100%'?

units.meaning: The Sun's 99.86% share is vastly larger than all other solar system mass combined, which is only 0.14%.
accepted_routes: The Sun outweighs the rest of the solar system combined.
The Sun's share (99.86%) is vastly larger than everything else combined (0.14%).
Sun mass is greater than all other solar system mass put together.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A Sun segment must be visibly contrasted against a much smaller non-Sun segment, not just shown as a standalone 99.86% label.
units.temporal_anchor: final clause, supported by the preceding contrast with Jupiter and the claim that the Sun is massive.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly compare the Sun against all other mass combined, or is the 99.86% share alone sufficient?

optional_valid: Rounding the Sun's 99.86% share to 100% for dramatic emphasis, provided the exact 99.86% is also available.
Calling the non-Sun mass a tiny rounding-error remainder, without adding new numeric claims.
Saying the Sun is the overwhelming majority of solar system mass.
unsupported_to_avoid: Jupiter's specific mass, mass share, or numeric comparison to the Sun; the table has no Jupiter row.
Sun mass in kilograms or Earth-mass equivalents; not in the table.
Claiming 99.86% refers to volume, diameter, or mass outside the solar system.
Causal claims that this mass dominance explains planetary formation, orbits, or fusion.
Saying all planets alone are 0.14%; the table's remainder is all non-Sun mass, not a planet-only breakdown.
notes: Only one table row is provided: the Sun's 99.86% mass share and its decimal equivalent. Derived units use arithmetic on that row; avoid Jupiter-specific numbers because the table has no Jupiter row.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
